title: Fix event listeners that do not fire
when: A click, submit, input or key handler does nothing, fires twice, or stops working after the list re-renders.
inputs: the HTML and the script that attaches the handler
prompt:
Goal: Every handler is attached once to an element that exists, with the right event name, and survives re-rendering.
Steps:
1. Confirm the script runs after the elements exist: defer, type="module", or code inside DOMContentLoaded.
2. Check the selector matches exactly one intended element (ids are unique, classes spelled right).
3. Check the event name: click, submit on the form (not the button), input for live typing, keydown for keys.
4. For items added later, use delegation: one listener on the stable parent and event.target.closest(".item") inside.
5. Look for blockers: an overlay with higher z-index, pointer-events: none, a disabled button, or a form reload without preventDefault.
6. Attach listeners in one setup function called once, so re-render code never adds duplicates.
Quality bar:
- Listeners live in script, not inline attributes.
- Delegated handlers ignore clicks outside items.
- Form handlers call preventDefault only when handling the submit in script.
Pitfalls:
- Calling the handler instead of passing it (addEventListener("click", save())).
- Re-adding listeners on every render, firing many times.
- Listening for click on a form for keyboard submit.
Verify:
- [ ] The handler fires once per action.
- [ ] It still works after items are added or removed.
- [ ] No inline on attributes remain for this feature.
- [ ] Files parse.
Output: The fixed script (and HTML if attributes change), plus the cause in one line.

examples.input: o botão de excluir não funciona nos itens novos
examples.output: one delegated listener on #list using closest(".delete"), set up once at start
